**Job Title:** Watt Outreach Navigator / Case Manager

**Program:** Watt / Weather Response

**Reports To:** Watt WR Program Manager

**FLSA Status:** Non-Exempt

**Revision Date:** October 2026

**Shift:** Day, as scheduled

**Summary:**

Working as part of a team, the Watt Outreach Navigator serves as a bridge between First Step Communities, persons experiencing or at risk of homelessness, the Watt Weather Response, surrounding businesses, community partners, and homeless service providers throughout Sacramento County. This position combines community outreach with short-term case management and client navigation. The Navigator builds relationships through street outreach, engagement in and around homeless encampments, referrals, and other community-based interactions; assesses client needs; and assists with connections to shelter, housing, long-term case management, behavioral health, substance use, and other supportive services. The Navigator also serves as a liaison to surrounding businesses, responds to homelessness-related concerns, provides information regarding available resources, and works toward constructive solutions. Using a Trauma-Informed, culturally responsive, and client-centered approach, the Navigator builds rapport and works collaboratively to guide clients toward positive outcomes.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities:**

Include the following. Specific duties may vary. Other duties may be assigned.

* Maintain continuity of care for individuals served through Watt Weather Response after the temporary shelter program is deactivated. Continue outreach, navigation, and short-term case management with assigned clients during periods when the Weather Response shelter is not active.
* Manage assigned clients and provide short-term case management and navigation services.
* Build rapport, provide support, and empower clients to participate in identifying goals and solutions.
* Conduct street outreach in encampments and other community-based settings.
* Conduct needs assessments and connect clients to shelter, housing, behavioral health, substance use, medical, benefits, and other supportive services.
* Respond to Sacramento 2-1-1 and other community or program referrals as assigned.
* Assist with Sacramento County shelter assessment and coordinated access programs and provide information on CORE and other appropriate resources.
* Manage multiple referrals, service connections, follow-up activities, and client progress simultaneously.
* Accurately document client contacts, services, referrals, resources, follow-up actions, and outcomes in HMIS and other required program records.
* Complete required chart audits, reports, and other program documentation.
* Work collaboratively with partner agencies, shelters, clinical staff, outreach teams, and other community organizations.
* Work in partner agencies, drop-in centers, shelters, community locations, and homeless encampments.
* Serve as a resource for clients, Navigators, shelter staff, clinical staff, and community partners.
* Serve as the primary liaison between Watt Weather Response and surrounding business owners.
* Address concerns involving unhoused individuals near businesses and communicate available shelter services, resources, outreach efforts, and potential solutions.
* Educate business owners and community members about programs and resources for persons experiencing homelessness.
* Foster positive relationships with the unhoused population and business community.
* Address business complaints or concerns constructively and professionally and provide appropriate follow-up.
* When appropriate, respectfully engage individuals congregating or loitering near businesses and encourage participation in available resources.
* Maintain clear and consistent professional boundaries while preserving positive client and community relationships.
* Use de-escalation, crisis intervention, problem-solving, decision-making, and critical-thinking skills in stressful situations.
* Maintain confidentiality and comply with program, agency, HMIS, and client privacy requirements.
* Participate in meetings, trainings, case conferences, and other program activities.
* Work collaboratively as part of the First Step Communities team.
* Perform other duties as assigned.

The Navigator will maintain an assigned caseload based on program needs and staffing levels.

**Supervisory Responsibilities:**

This position may be subject to staff supervisory responsibilities.

The employee must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The listed requirements represent the knowledge, skills, and abilities required for the position.

High school diploma or GED is required. Sixty (60) units or more of college beyond high school is strongly preferred; a bachelor's degree in social work or a related field is preferred. Experience working with unsheltered individuals experiencing complex needs, including mental health and/or alcohol and other drug symptoms or behaviors, is desirable. jobs.description:
Habitat Health empowers older adults to experience more good days in their homes and communities. Through the Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly (PACE), we provide comprehensive medical care along with support for daily needs such as meals, transportation, and in‑home assistance. We deliver coordinated clinical and social care in our centers and directly in participants' homes, creating a fully integrated experience that brings peace of mind and a true sense of belonging. As we expand our scalable, affordable PACE model to meet the growing and complex needs of aging populations, our mission‑driven care teams continue to help participants live well on their own terms.

Habitat Health is supported by leading healthcare organizations and investors including New Enterprise Associates, Kaiser Permanente, and Town Hall Ventures. We are entering a period of significant growth and are looking for exceptional teammates to help us scale a better model of care for older adults. To learn more, visit www.habitathealth.com.

**Estimated Start Date:** 11/2026

**Schedule:** Monday - Friday

**Location:** Sacramento Center

**Role Scope**:

The RN Care Manager delivers personalized, longitudinal nursing care to a panel of PACE participants, conducting face-to-face assessments across physical, psychosocial, and behavioral domains in both center and home settings, and partnering with medical providers to implement care plans. This role manages care coordination end-to-end, collaborating and coordinating with the entire care team as needed. As a collaborative participant and leader in Interdisciplinary Team (IDT) meetings, this role contributes clinical insights that inform whole-person care planning and educates participants, caregivers, and team members on carrying out personalized care plans — all while contributing to a center culture grounded in Habitat's values and participant belonging

**Core Responsibilities & Expectations for the Role**

* Contribute to a center experience that Participants want to spend time in, a team culture that cares and creates joy, and an environment where all participants and team members belong.
* Continue to raise the bar. Constructively seek and share feedback and help us implement changes in order to improve clinical outcomes and experience for participants.
* Exhibit and honor Habitat's Values.
* Participate n Interdisciplinary Team (IDT) meetings by contributing insights from assessments, care plan recommendations, and care coordination in a collaborative spirit.
* Conduct face-to-face nursing assessments that are inclusive of physical, psychosocial, and behavioral statuses in various settings, primarily in the Habitat center but also in–home as needed.
* In partnership with a medical provider, deliver personalized care for a panel of participants based on care plans.
* Deliver and document nursing interventions as agreed upon in participant's care plans, promptly and accurately responding to physician orders, and correctly administering medications and therapeutic interventions.
* Provide case management longitudinally and during transitions of care. Proactively coordinate complex patient discharges, transfers, and immediate post-discharge needs with hospital and long-term care facility case managers.
* Coordinate all aspects of care delivery including medication. management, medical equipment and supplies, and specialist and diagnostic referrals
* Triage in the outpatient setting, which includes independently initiating therapies within scope of practice and collaboratively working with a medical provider to escalate care as needed.
* Educate participants, caregivers including family members, and team members on how to personalize and carry out care plans.
* Aid with all wound care (including complex wounds), IV (hydration, therapies), and any additional procedures within RN scope of practice identified to meet evolving participant needs.
* Delegate tasks to MA and Licensed Vocational Nurses within their respective scopes of practice.
* Option to participate in after-hour calls that are triaged on a rotating schedule for extra compensation.
* Perform related duties as assigned.

**Required Qualifications:**

* Graduate of an accredited school of nursing or equivalent experience.
* Unencumbered California Registered Nurse (RN) license required.
* Minimum 2-4 years of experience clinically caring for medically complex or older adults' population as an RN.
* Minimum 1-2 year's experience in case management.
* Strong clinical acumen in chronic disease management and complex geriatric care.
* Demonstrates experience in management of clinical interventions: wound care, IVs, phlebotomy, colostomy/ileostomy care, etc.
* Proof of current CPR/BLS certification required or requirement to obtain within 30 days of employment.
* A minimum of one year experience working with the frail or elderly.
* Aligns with our purpose and our values, and is excited about living those out in daily practice
* Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, evolving environment with comfort navigating ambiguity, adapting quickly, and contributing to continuous improvement.
* Strong learning and growth mindset, including seeking feedback, engaging in healthy debate and using data and curiosity to inform decisions.
* Acts with integrity and ownership, considering the broader organizational impact, doing the right thing, and following through to deliver results.

**Nice to have:**

* Bachelor's of Science (BSN) preferred.
* Bilingual: Spanish/English preferred.
* PACE experience and/ or ADCH/CBAS experience.
* A state issued driver's license, personal transportation, and auto insurance as required by law.

jobs.description:
**About AEG:**

At AEG, we're building something bigger than great eye care, we're creating careers, developing leaders, and making a meaningful difference in the communities we serve.

You'll join a team that:

* Invests in leadership development and internal growth.
* Believes people and performance go hand in hand.
* Values collaboration, authenticity, and continuous learning.
* Celebrates wins, supports challenges, and grows together.

**About the role**

At AEG, we believe great patient experiences begin with great teams. As a Patient Care Coordinator you are responsible not only for front desk operations, but also for supporting patient flow, schedule optimization, and seamless coordination across the care team.

The ability to anticipate needs, communicate clearly, and proactively manage the daily schedule helps ensure an efficient, high-quality experience for every patient.

  

* Greet patients, customers, and vendors in a friendly, professional, and welcoming manner; serve as the primary point of contact for patient interactions.
* Answer telephone calls, respond to inquiries, and manage email or digital communications in a timely and professional manner.
* Schedule patient appointments while supporting provider schedule optimization, including managing cancellations, reschedules, and same-day fill opportunities.
* Execute appointment confirmation and reminder processes to reduce no-show rates and ensure patients are prepared for their visit.
* Verify insurance eligibility and patient demographics prior to appointments; accurately enter and maintain complete information in EMR.
* Maintain a clear understanding of insurance plans and effectively communicate coverage, benefits, and patient financial responsibility.
* Prepare patient charts and required documentation in advance of visits to support efficient patient flow.
* Collect and document all charges, co-pays, and payments into EMR; allocate balances appropriately and support claim preparation and submission.
* Run reports and review accounts to ensure all charges are billed, filed, and up to date.
* Monitor daily patient flow and provider schedules to identify bottlenecks, delays, or overlaps; communicate and adjust as needed to support efficient patient flow.
* Proactively communicate with patients regarding wait times, delays, and next steps to maintain a positive experience.
* Coordinate with clinical and optical teams to ensure smooth patient transitions and continuity of care throughout the visit.
* Support patient retention efforts through follow-up, recall, and reactivation outreach, including annual and medically necessary appointments.
* Assist in maintaining an organized, clean, and patient-ready front office environment.
* Perform other duties as needed and as assigned by the Practice Manager, Assistant Practice Manager and/or Optometrist.

Requirements:

* High school diploma or equivalent.
* Basic computer literacy and ability to learn practice management systems (EMR).
* Strong organizational skills with attention to detail and ability to manage multiple priorities.
* Strong communication skills (verbal and written) with a focus on patient-centered service.
* Strong interpersonal skills and ability to work collaboratively across teams.
* Ability to proactively identify issues and contribute to solutions in a fast-paced environment.
* Must be able to maintain patient and practice confidentiality.

**Full Time Employee Benefits**

* 401(k) with Match
* Medical/Dental/Vision/Life/STD/LTD
* Employee Vision Discount Program
* HSA/FSA
* PTO
* Paid Holidays

**Physical Demands**

* Ability to utilize office equipment
* Prolonged sitting, standing, and walking
* Ability to lift up to 10 lbs

Do you want to be part of an innovative organization sustaining vulnerable, isolated seniors to EAT: Eat, Age, Thrive in Yolo County and regionally? Is the “why” you do your job a priority in your career? Then you may be the hero we’re seeking to provide nourishing meals and wellness checks to aging adults countywide and beyond lacking the access and/or the ability to dependably prepare their own healthy meals.  
  
MOW YOLO APPROACH  
Meals on Wheels Yolo County (“MOW Yolo”) is adding a Community Health Worker to our already inspired team. We are looking for a CHW who will:  

* Lead efforts with MOW Yolo seniors to identify their needs and connect them with appropriate resources and services.
* Prioritize nutritious food security and socialization so that seniors in the region may EAT: Eat, Age, Thrive.
* Positively represent MOW Yolo internally and externally

  
POSITION SUMMARY:  
The Community Health Worker (CHW) reports to the Programs Director and provides compassionate, person-centered support to seniors, ages 60 and older. The work of the CHW furthers MOW Yolo’s mission to nourish and engage vulnerable older adults and others with mobility challenges throughout Yolo County and beyond.  
  
USUAL WORK SCHEDULE:  
The CHW is a full-time (40 hours per week), non-exempt position, working Monday through Friday, 9:00am-5:00pm with some flexibility available based upon organizational needs. Primary work location is in the field at MOW Yolo Participant homes, congregate meal locations, and other sites throughout Yolo County, including the MOW Yolo Administrative office in Woodland and the MOW Yolo meal production facility in Winters.  
  
ESSENTIAL JOB DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:  
1. Participant Intake & Assessment: Conduct person-centered assessments to identify participants’ needs, strengths, barriers, and goals.  
2. Participant Support & Follow-Up: Manage an assigned caseload of seniors, conduct regular check-ins and reassessments, and coordinate ongoing services to support health, independence, and safe aging in place.  
3. Resource Coordination & Referrals: Connect participants with appropriate community resources and supportive services, assist with referrals as needed, and maintain an up-to-date directory of senior-focused resources.  
4. Relationship Building & Community Engagement: Develop positive relationships with seniors, caregivers, volunteers, colleagues, and community partners while participating in outreach and strengthening awareness of MOW Yolo programs and services.  
5. Documentation, Communication & Professional Responsibilities: Maintain accurate case records and required documentation, communicate participant needs and emerging issues with supervisors and colleagues, attend staff meetings, and support evolving program needs.  
6. Supervise Community Navigator(s) in shared work responsibilities.  
  
QUALIFICATIONS:  
1. Education & Experience: High school diploma or equivalent required; Associate’s Degree in a related field preferred. Experience working with seniors and knowledge of aging-related needs preferred; outreach experience desirable.  
2. Physical Requirements: Ability to lift and carry up to 50 lbs., stand for extended periods, bend below the waist, and reach overhead.  
3. Independent & Adaptive Work: Ability to work independently with minimal supervision and respond flexibly, creatively, and patiently to varied and unexpected situations.  
4. Communication & Technology Skills: Ability to read, write, perform basic math, and accurately maintain records and reports. Proficiency with or willingness to learn electronic systems; Microsoft Office experience required, with Google Workspace familiarity preferred.  
5. Driving & Professional Standards: Valid California Class C driver’s license with a satisfactory driving record, maintained in good standing. Demonstrates professional hygiene, appearance, conduct, and demeanor.  
  
POSITION LICENSES/CERTIFICATIONS:  
1. Current California Driver’s License.  
2. Proof of current automobile insurance.  
3. Mandated Reporter Training, Mental Health First Aid Cert, BLS, Motivational Interviewing, (MOW Yolo pays for this training if needed).  
  
COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS  
$26-$30 per hour (DOE), payable per the regular payroll schedule and subject to applicable withholding and payroll taxes and other deductions required by law. Full-time employees receive paid medical, dental, vision, vacation and sick time accrual, 11 paid holidays annually, and the option to participate in a 401(k) Retirement Savings Plan.  
  
\*\*This position is funded through a grant and is contingent upon the availability and continuation of grant funding.\*\*  
  
APPLICATION PROCEDURE AND TIMELINE  
Please submit your resume to HR@mowyolo.org. Applicant screening will be ongoing as the goal is to  
welcome a new team member as soon as possible.  
  
ABOUT MEALS ON WHEELS YOLO COUNTY  
Meals on Wheels Yolo County has a 50-year history as the only provider of fully-prepared meals for food insecure, isolated seniors in Yolo County, now nourishing 1,000 aging adults in both the cities and rural communities, as well as hundreds more regionally as part of MOW Yolo’s growing social enterprise operations. Core programs include:  

* Home-Delivered Meals (primarily volunteer delivered)
* Café Yolo Social Dining (congregate meals)
* Weekend Food Project (shelf-stable meals)
* MOW PAWS - Pets and Well Seniors (pet foods for isolated seniors’ furry companions)

MOW Yolo performs its mission according to a three-year strategic plan and sparks and engages in dozens of collaborations and partnerships throughout the region to sustain and elevate the opportunity for seniors to EAT: Eat, Age, Thrive and age in place healthily and safely, with independence and dignity.

**Responsibilities:**

* Interview members to assess medical and social determinant of healthcare gaps and provide education about their condition and medication, while developing individualized care plans.

* **Individuals experiencing homelessness:** Lacking a fixed, regular, and adequate nighttime residence.

* **Individuals at risk for avoidable hospital or emergency department utilization:** Five or more emergency room visits in a six-month period that could have been avoided with appropriate outpatient care or improved treatment adherence.

* **Individuals transitioning from incarceration/Justice Involved:** Adults transitioning from a correctional setting or transitioned from a correction setting within the past 12 months, or children and youth who are transitioning from a youth correctional facility or transitioned from being in a youth correctional facility within the past 12 months.

* **Pregnant and Postpartum individuals; Birth Equity Population of Focus:** Adults and youth who are pregnant or postpartum and qualify for eligibility in any other adult or youth ECM POF, or are subject to racial and ethnic disparities.

* Minimum of 1 year experience in case management, member care, customer

**Summary:** The Case Manager Registered Nurse is responsible for coordinating care for diverse, high-risk, and complex patients transitioning from acute care settings. RN Case Manager Duties:

Patient Care& Education

* Oversee and facilitate the transition of care for high-risk patients, ensuring continuity and quality from acute settings to home or community resources.
* Collaborate with patients, families, and interdisciplinary team members to develop individualized care plans for complex and high risk patients.

* Document phone triage assessments appropriately in the electronic medical record
* Document and reports malfunction of PHC equipment
* Maintain a clean, orderly and functional work environment
* Promote continuous improvement of workplace safety and environmental practices

Training:

* Mentor and orient new staff, students and other team members

* Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) preferred
* At least one year of experience in case management nursing within a healthcare setting focused on high-risk populations preferred

* Active State of California Registered Nurse (RN) License in good standing required
* Valid State of California Driver’ s License (DL) in good standing required
* Current Basic Life Support (BLS) certificate required
* Candidate must be able to successfully meet PHC’s credentialing and privileging requirements

**Language Skills**: Bilingual in English and Spanish, both written and verbal preferred. Assessed by language proficiency test as Advanced or Intermediate level.

Valeris works on behalf of life sciences companies to improve the patient experience so that patients can access and adhere to critical medications. Backed by proven industry expertise, a deep commitment to patient care, the latest technology, and exceptionally talented team members, Valeris provides the data and strategic insights, patient support services and healthcare provider engagement tools to help life sciences companies successfully commercialize new products. Valeris provides commercialization solutions to more than 500 life sciences customers and has provided access and affordability support to millions of patients. The company is headquartered in Morrisville, North Carolina and Jeffersonville, Indiana. To learn more about Valeris, please visit www.valeris.com.

Valeris will be hiring for a **Care Coordinator** in the near future and are proactively building our pipeline of qualified candidates. **Key Responsibilities:**
-------------------------

The responsibilities include, but are not limited to the following:

  

* Relationship Management
  + Builds trusted relationships with patients, prescribers, client stakeholders through proactive communication, timely and accurate execution of deliverables and demonstrated relentless passion for helping patients
  + Manages all relationships in a manner that adheres to healthcare laws and regulations
* Communications
  + Performs program welcome calls to patients
  + Performs post Benefits Investigation calls to patients and physicians explaining coverage optionsManages all client inquiries unable to be determined by client through reportingManages HCP inquiries, as applicable, pursuant to business rules
* Inbound Call Management
  + Manages inbound calls as directed by the program-approved FAQs
  + Triage patients to internal or external resources as appropriate

  + Provides personalized case management to patients and HCPs including outbound communication to HCPs and patients to communicate benefit coverage and next steps in obtaining coverage

  + Coordinates nurse teach with field-based nurse educators, as applicable to program
  + Supports adherence services through coordination of nurse follow up, as applicable to program
  + Identifies peer support resources for patients
  + Coordinates shipment of product through patient assistance program and/or bridge program from the PharmaCord pharmacy
  + Proactively communicates needs for reverification of prior authorization or re-enrollment for patient assistance program
  + Reports adverse events, Product complaints, special situation reports and/or medical inquiries received in accordance with SOPs and the Business Rules
  + Documents all activities within the PharmaCord Lynk system in accordance with business requirements
  + Utilize Valeris’ values as the driving force behind the team’s success
  + On time adherence to training deadlines for all corporate policies and procedures
  + Ensure all SOPs are followed with consistencyPerform additional tasks or projects as assigned
